title: The Sunrise
content:
The morning was wrapped in a peaceful silence as the first rays of sunlight slipped through the clouds. A train raced north from Kochi to Delhi, carrying hundreds of passengers toward different destinations. None of them knew that this ordinary journey was about to become the beginning of an extraordinary love story.

Inside one of the train's quiet coaches, the sharp buzz of a phone shattered the peaceful silence. A delicate hand reached out from beneath the blanket, searching blindly until it found the vibrating phone. Still lost in sleep, she answered with a faint yawn.

"Hello... who's speaking?"

"It's your mother," came the familiar voice from the other end.

A few seconds passed before she realized who was on the other end of the call. The drowsiness vanished from her face almost instantly, replaced by a warm smile.

"Good morning, Mom," she said, her voice now much more cheerful.

"Don't tell me you're still sleeping!" her mother exclaimed. "It's already ten o'clock."

She let out a soft yawn and leaned back against her berth. "Mom, I still have two whole days before I reach Delhi. Let me sleep a little longer."

"Wake up, you lazy girl," her mother scolded playfully. "Aren't you ashamed of saying that?"

A gentle smile curved across the girl's lips. She had heard those words countless times, yet they never failed to make her smile.

"Okay, okay, Mom," she laughed. "Don't shout. I'm getting up."

"That's better," her mother replied before ending the conversation.

The girl slipped her phone into her pocket and stretched lazily, trying to shake off the last traces of sleep. Drawn by the cool morning breeze, she made her way toward the train's open doorway.

As the wind brushed against her face, a few loose strands of her long, silky hair danced gracefully in the air. She absentmindedly tucked them behind her ear, unaware that a single glance at her could steal anyone's attention. Her radiant smile, adorned with two adorable dimples, had a charm that could make even the moon feel envious.

She was twenty-two years old, blessed with porcelain-white skin that seemed to glow beneath the gentle morning sunlight. There was a quiet elegance in the way she carried herself—effortless, graceful, and impossible to ignore. Her soft features, expressive eyes, and innocent smile blended into a beauty that was both captivating and comforting, leaving an unforgettable impression on everyone who crossed her path.

After enjoying the cool breeze for a while, she returned to her seat, resting her chin against the window as the train continued its journey.

The train gradually slowed as it approached Bengaluru Junction. With a gentle screech of its brakes, it came to a halt, and the peaceful atmosphere was instantly replaced by the lively bustle of the platform. Passengers hurried through the doors carrying suitcases, backpacks, and bags, while vendors called out to attract customers one last time before departure.

One after another, the new passengers stepped into the coach, searching for their reserved seats. Conversations filled the air as luggage was tucked beneath berths and overhead racks. Although many seats were occupied, nearly half of the coach still remained empty, leaving the compartment surprisingly spacious.

A few minutes later, a long whistle echoed across the station. The train shuddered gently before slowly pulling away from the platform, leaving Bengaluru behind as it resumed its journey toward Delhi.

Curious about the people who would accompany her for the next two days, the girl quietly glanced around the compartment. Her eyes soon fell upon a little boy sitting directly opposite her, nestled comfortably between his mother and father. The child looked no older than five, his bright, innocent eyes wandering around the coach with endless curiosity.

A gentle smile blossomed across her face as she watched him. The little boy noticed her almost immediately and blinked back with the same innocent wonder that only children possess.

She couldn't help but smile a little wider before turning her gaze back toward the window. Beyond the glass, endless green fields stretched into the distance, swaying gently beneath the warm morning sun as the train raced through the heart of the countryside.

Just as she lost herself in the endless landscape beyond the window, a dull thud echoed through the coach—the unmistakable sound of a travel bag hitting the floor.

The unexpected noise pulled her attention away from the passing scenery. She turned instinctively toward the aisle.

A young man stood there, bending down to pick up the bag that had slipped from his hand. He was dressed in a neatly fitted black shirt and grey trousers, with a pair of earphones tucked into his ears. Completely unaware of the eyes fixed upon him, he dusted off the bag and adjusted its torn handle before looking around for his seat.

For a brief moment, the world around her faded into silence.

There was something effortlessly captivating about him. His gentle expression, sharp features, and the calm confidence with which he carried himself made it impossible for her to look away. She had seen countless handsome faces before, but none had stirred her heart the way his did.

As he began walking down the aisle, her eyes followed him without hesitation.

Please... let his seat be next to mine, she silently prayed, her fingers unconsciously tightening around the edge of her berth.

He drew closer.

One row...

Then another...

Her heartbeat quickened with every step he took.

But instead of stopping beside her, he walked past her seat and continued toward the rear of the coach.

The tiny spark of hope in her heart quietly faded.

She let out an almost inaudible sigh before forcing a smile at herself. It was strange. This was the first time a man had left such an impression on her. Over the years, she had received more proposals than she could count, yet she had never once been tempted to accept any of them. Love had always seemed distant—something that happened to other people.

Yet now, after nothing more than a single glance, a complete stranger had managed to leave her utterly captivated.

Shaking her head, she tried to dismiss the unfamiliar feeling with a quiet smile.

"Look at him... someone that handsome is probably already committed," she murmured to herself, turning back toward the window, though her thoughts stubbornly refused to leave him.

A few minutes drifted by, and the peaceful rhythm of the train slowly began to feel monotonous. Unable to sit still any longer, she decided to stretch her legs and enjoy the cool breeze from the train's doorway.

She rose from her seat and walked leisurely down the aisle. As she passed the entrance to the adjacent compartment, her curiosity got the better of her. She stole a quick glance inside.

There he was.

He was seated just a few rows behind her compartment.

A wave of excitement rushed through her heart. She had thought he had gone much farther down the train, but fate had placed him much closer than she had imagined. She instinctively quickened her pace toward the doorway, unable to hide the smile that found its way onto her lips.

As she stood by the open door, the cool wind brushed against her face, but her thoughts remained fixed on the young man she had just seen.

There was something about him that caught her attention this time—not his appearance, but his expression.

His face carried a quiet sadness, as though something weighed heavily on his mind. Even from a distance, she could sense the loneliness hidden behind his composed demeanour.

She found herself wondering what could have happened.

"Maybe he had an argument with his girlfriend," she thought, letting out a faint sigh. "Someone like him must already have someone in his life."

The thought brought a strange ache to her heart, one she couldn't quite understand.

Still, a tiny part of her wished for something impossible.

"God... if it's meant to happen, at least let us talk once before this journey ends."

A gentle breeze swept past her as the train sped forward, carrying with it a silent prayer that only her heart could hear.
